blocks.hero.eyebrow: EMDR therapy · Louisville, KY and online
blocks.hero.subhead: Some memories keep hitting with the same force, no matter how long ago they happened. EMDR helps your mind and body stop reacting as though the danger is still here.

facts.text: You stay in control of the pace

blocks.request.heading: Healing can start at your pace
blocks.request.text: Request an appointment in about a minute, or call (502) 523-2970. Most people are seen the same week.

signs.items.text: A memory still feels present, in your body or your reactions.
Reminders bring back the same fear, shame, or panic every time.
Memories or nightmares come back without warning.
Talking about it hasn't made it lose its grip.
You've heard of EMDR and want to know if it could help.
You'd rather not have to describe everything in detail.

blocks.faith.heading: Faith at the center, never forced
blocks.faith.body: If you want faith to be part of your healing, including hard questions about safety, trust, and where God was in what happened, your counselor will bring it in. If not, that's entirely your call.

sections.heading: How EMDR therapy works
sections.body:
EMDR (eye movement desensitization and reprocessing) is a structured, well-researched therapy for trauma. While you briefly bring a painful memory to mind, your counselor guides you through eye movements or another back-and-forth rhythm. Over time, the memory tends to lose its emotional charge. It stays a memory, but it stops running your present.

You don't have to describe everything that happened in detail, the way some talk therapy asks you to.

sections.heading: You stay in control
sections.body: Before any memory work begins, your counselor helps you build safety and steadiness: tools to calm your body and stay grounded. You set the pace, and you can pause at any time. The goal is healing, never re-living the trauma.

sections.heading: If EMDR isn't the right fit
sections.body: EMDR is one way to heal from trauma, not the only one. Our counselors also work with trauma through other approaches, including internal family systems and acceptance and commitment therapy. See [trauma counseling](/trauma-counseling).

blocks.team.heading: Counselors who offer EMDR

team.items.text: EMDR in person or online, for trauma, grief, and painful memories, with a psychodynamic, trauma-focused approach.

blocks.expect.heading: Your first session
blocks.expect.body: Your first session focuses on getting to know you and building safety, not on the trauma itself. You won't be asked to go into detail before you're ready. EMDR sessions are in our Middletown office or online.
blocks.cost.body: $100 per session. We don't bill insurance, but we'll give you a superbill to submit for possible out-of-network reimbursement.
blocks.team.note: EMDR is offered by Staci and Kasie, both EMDR-trained. If EMDR isn't the right fit for you, trauma counseling with ACT and IFS is another path.
